speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Firms have also received support for their manpower costs through the Jobs Support Scheme and Foreign Worker Levy waivers and rebates.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: The Government has also put in place unprecedented legislative measures through the COVID-19 (Temporary Measures) Act, or COTMA, to provide relief for contractors and to enable equitable co-sharing of increased costs by project parties due to the pandemic.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: These measures have helped the construction industry tide over the COVID-19 pandemic.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: We do not take decisions to intervene in private contracts lightly.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: The COTMA reliefs are meant to be temporary and firms will need to partner one another for long-term sustainability and resilience.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: However, given the significant impact of COVID-19 on the Built Environment (BE) sector, we have extended the relevant COTMA reliefs several times.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: This has provided firms with additional time and support to negotiate amicable outcomes between the parties.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: And we have seen encouraging signs of the sector’s recovery.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Based on project progress payments made at the industry level, the current level of construction output is close to pre-COVID-19 levels.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: This indicates that construction works are progressing at a steady state.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: We strongly encourage all contracting parties to agree on mutually beneficial arrangements to sustain their projects.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: While the foreign manpower inflow has been improving in recent months, we will continue to monitor the situation and review whether a further extension is needed.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The progress that the Minister of State mentioned is good news, especially if COTMA is going to be tapered off this year.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: But I have a bit of concern in terms of expectations of disputes probably going up later this year, especially between contractors and their respective employers.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: So, my first question is whether there will be any low-cost ways for these firms to resolve disputes going forward, especially if measures taper?

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: On the first point, I would just like to assure the Member that we are very focused on this issue, making sure that the construction works in the BE sector proceed safely and seamlessly.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: There are very important public sector projects, from housing to transportation, to private residential projects that we know are important to Singaporeans and we want to make sure the construction works continue smoothly and safely and that the entire sector is on a steady keel.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: We have been in regular contact with the construction industry, the BE sector, from developers to consultants, architects, engineers, contractors, facility managers, companies big and small.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: All the Government agencies, the Government procurement entities, like HDB and LTA, have been working very closely with their contractors and their subcontractors, making sure that work continues.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: So, I would just like to reassure the Member that we are monitoring the situation very closely.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: In fact, my colleagues from MOM and MND meet these firms on a very regular basis, going through issues of payment, workers, inflow of workers, salaries and so on.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: On a related second point around the movement of workers, we have been working together with the Singapore Contractors' Association Limited, or SCAL, to look at different mechanisms.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: We are also in close contact with the various firms through the Association.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: These are issues that we are working on very closely and we will monitor the situation in the coming months.
